resources.string: Emufii: Azahar and Eden netplay filling
Lets Emufii fill in the connection address in Azahar\'s or Eden\'s multiplayer menu, so you don\'t have to retype it. Emufii only watches those two emulators, and only while a session is running.
Pick the folder your ROMs are in. Subfolders are scanned too, whichever console they hold.
It won\'t show in the session list: people will need your code to get in.
It will show in the session list, where anyone can join it.
The game opens on its own
You play online, nothing to set up
Emufii opens a session and gives you a code
Your friends type it in to join you
The consoles see each other as on local Wi-Fi
You play with strangers, on a public server run by third parties. Emufii creates no session and brings up no tunnel: it opens PPSSPP, and PPSSPP is what connects you.
To do, once and for all
Open PPSSPP with the button below, then go to Settings → Networking.
Turn networking on, and pick a public server from the list PPSSPP keeps up to date.
Leave “Try to use the server’s packet relay” on Automatic: that is what public servers want. Set it back to Disabled if you come back to play with friends.
Come back here and launch the game, then take its ad hoc mode.
1. Open PPSSPP to set up online play
Allow Emufii to install apps in your Android settings.
This version isn\'t downloadable here yet.
Download interrupted. Try again, the file is there.
File rejected: it isn\'t signed like this app.
Emufii creates no session: this mode does not go through it.
Emufii opens PPSSPP for you to set up, then the game, in that order.
In the game, take ad hoc mode: you land among the players already connected.
Share it, or let your friends find you in the open sessions.
DS online play doesn\'t go through a session
Multiplayer isn\'t supported for this console yet
DS online play starts from the library, not from a session
No ROM attached to this session
Emufii opens multiplayer and fills the address in for you.

Before you play, set your name by hand in Azahar → Settings and system: it needs at least 5 characters. Emufii leaves it alone, and Azahar refuses the room when the name is too short, blaming the address, which is fine.
Open the menu → Multiplayer, then enter %1$s.
Emufii can no longer reach the session server: the player list below is from the last answer we got. The tunnel itself is holding: a game already running keeps running. Check your connection.
You\'re in the session and on the same network, but Emufii couldn\'t find this game on your device. Add it to your ROMs folder, rescan, then come back.
In PPSSPP, once and for all
PPSSPP cannot be driven by Emufii: it draws its own interface. These four settings are yours to make, once, and never again.
Networking → Ad hoc server address → Add server → paste %1$s
Just below it: “Try to use the server’s packet relay” set to Disabled
PPSSPP says so itself: that mode is for when a public server relays packets for you. Here your consoles talk to each other directly: it has nothing to do.
Networking → Enable built-in ad hoc server
System → Nickname: yours, Emufii never touches it

This is the one setting that really changes how the game feels, and it is not in the emulator. Measured on a real match: a player sitting far from their router sends packets in bursts instead of a steady stream, and it shows up on screen as stutter. Same player, closer in, and it is gone. Prefer 5 GHz over 2.4, and turn power saving off.
This address never changes: the relay sends it to whoever is hosting your session, game after game.
You both need the exact same version of the game, updates and DLC included. A version that differs on one side stops the game, usually without saying why: the room joins, then nothing starts.
Eden\'s multiplayer lives in its settings, not in the game: ⚙ Settings → Multiplayer → “Create”. You can open it before or during play.
Eden\'s multiplayer lives in its settings, not in the game: ⚙ Settings → Multiplayer → “Join”. You can open it before or during play.
Emufii fills the address, the port and your nickname in for you as soon as the dialog opens.
Your Emufii nickname is copied into Eden: two players with the same nickname cannot share a room, and Eden gives everyone the same one by default.
DS online play doesn\'t work by session: each console dials the revival server, there is no network to share. Go back to the library and start the game from there.
The game is in your library, but Emufii doesn\'t know how to set up multiplayer for this console yet. The session network is up: go ahead if your emulator can make use of it.
No open sessions. Start yours from your library and it will show up here for everyone else.
This can take 10-15 s the first time.
Your photo stays on your phone. Other players see your initials and your colour.
What everyone else sees in the session.
Subfolders are scanned too, whichever console they hold.
No keys. Switch and Wii games keep their initials.
Keys in place. Switch icons are being read.
Emufii ships no keys and downloads none: point it at your own prod.keys, the one your Switch emulator already uses. It stays on your phone.
That file does not hold the expected keys.

Emufii sets up remote multiplayer between emulators: it shares a network, it doesn\'t reimplement any game. Distributed under the AGPL 3.0 licence, it never routes to Nintendo\'s official servers and ships no ROMs, no BIOS and no keys.
Emufii can fill the address into the emulator\'s multiplayer menu, so you have nothing to copy out.
Emufii cannot fill the emulator\'s form in. Sessions still work, the address just has to be typed by hand.
Android can switch it off on its own, after an update or a change of device. This is where it goes back on.
Too many attempts, try again in a minute
Without VPN permission, Emufii cannot bring the network up
Session not found, the code may have expired
Emufii can\'t reach its server. Check your connection and try again.
This session is for %1$s. Join it with that game.
The host has not finished connecting
Without VPN permission, Emufii cannot join
DS online play is holding the tunnel, and Android allows only one. Continuing will cut the redirection to Kaeru: a DS game in progress would be interrupted.
A session is still open and holding the tunnel, and Android allows only one. Continuing will close it.
The previous tunnel did not stop

Nintendo\'s servers have been off since 2014. Kaeru WFC is a third-party reimplementation that replays the original protocol. Emufii points melonDS\'s lookups at it, and nothing else on the device is affected.
Kaeru isn\'t answering, the game won\'t be able to connect
Without the VPN the console will go to Nintendo\'s dead servers
Session tunnel status for remote multiplayer
DNS redirection for DS online play
This build of %1$s (%2$s) has no multiplayer. Update it to play online.
It identifies you to other players, and doubles as your pseudo in the emulator\'s multiplayer.
%1$d characters minimum: emulators reject a shorter name.
Emufii sets up remote multiplayer between emulators. It shares a network between your devices, then lets the emulator do the rest, as if you were in the same room.
Pick your ROMs folder. Subfolders are scanned too, whichever console they hold, keep your filing as it is.
Emufii shows the tunnel and local network status in a notification while you play inside the emulator. Without it, Android may cut the network when Emufii goes to the background.
Declined. You can turn it on later in Android\'s settings.
Azahar asks for the host\'s address and port by hand, every game. Allow Emufii and it types them for you. It only ever sees Azahar\'s screen, nothing else.
Give this code to someone so they can add you. It never changes, unless you reset your profile.
That code isn\'t valid. Check you copied all of it.
Swap codes with someone: you\'ll then see when they\'re playing, and join them in one tap.
Remove %1$s from your friends? You\'ll need their code to add them back.
Your friends list stays on your phone. The server only knows who is online, and forgets it after two minutes.
Delete your profile? This can\'t be undone: your friend code changes, and your friends list is erased.
ROMs only carry a 32 or 48 pixel icon. With a SteamGridDB key, the library fetches real, sharp ones.
Free key at steamgriddb.com, in your account preferences. Without it, the ROMs\' own icons stay.
ROMs only carry a tiny icon. A free SteamGridDB key replaces them with real game icons.
Create one at steamgriddb.com, in your account preferences. You can skip this and add it later in settings.
No icon for this game. Try another name: matching uses the file name, which isn\'t always the game\'s.
The game leaves Emufii\'s library. The file and its saves are untouched, and the settings bring everything back.
Removed games stay on your storage: only their tile is gone. Restoring puts them all back in the grid, in alphabetical place.
Inside Emufii only: the file on your storage is left alone. Leave empty to restore the original title.
Search a game, a player, a code
Open the room, then pick the game inside it: everyone starts it together.
Join the room, then wait for the host to pick the game. Do not start anything yourself.
You both need the exact same dump. Dolphin compares hashes and refuses otherwise.

You also need to start from the same save. If one of you is further along, the two games diverge the moment they start: each player sees a different match, with no error message. Safest is for neither of you to have a save at all.
Emufii fills in the address and port, sets the connection to direct, and points the room at the session\'s game.
In Dolphin, ⋮ menu then Netplay: direct connection, and enter %1$s.
The PS2 network profile is missing. Open Emufii\'s settings, "PS2 network profile": without it, no PS2 LAN game will open its local menu.

A PS2 LAN game only opens its local menu when the console has a network configuration on its memory card. Most games expect it without being able to create it. Emufii hands over a memory card that carries one. It is copy-protected, so it cannot join your usual card: your saves come to it instead.
Choose "Import file" and pick the file prepared above.
Put it in slot 1, and your old card in slot 2.
Boot the BIOS, then copy a game\'s data from card 2 onto card 1. Keep the old card: whatever is protected will never leave it.
Do not skip the last step: card 1 has to hold a game\'s data, or this will not work. Once it does, create your profiles straight on it, with no need to go back to your old card.
In the game, pick LAN, System Link or Network Play. You are the one opening the match.
Wait for the host to open their match, then join it from the game\'s LAN menu.
Only games that shipped with a LAN or System Link mode work here, around sixty in all. If the game asks you to sign in to a server, it was an online game, and Emufii cannot help with it.
With the network adapter attached, some games stop responding to the controller entirely. If that happens, turn DEV9 Ethernet off in ARMSX2.
Emufii turns DEV9 on, sets ARMSX2 to local mode, and fills in the address, port and room code.
In ARMSX2, Settings then Network: local mode, and enter %1$s.
These are the emulators that run the games, Emufii runs none itself. Turn a console off to take it out of your library, with its games.
Proven at the versions shown here.
